ing: bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick
st: Fry the onions in [[0.25 cup]] ghee over medium heat for 15 minutes until deep brown, then set half aside for layering.
Mix the chicken with the yogurt, garlic, ginger, chili, turmeric, [[2 tsp]] garam masala, [[2 tsp]] salt and half the mint.
Marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour.
In a heavy pot, heat [[2 tbsp]] ghee and add the whole spices, then the marinated chicken and tomatoes.
Cook 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and reaches 165°F (74°C).
Boil [[8 cups]] water with [[1 tsp]] salt and the drained rice for 6 minutes until 70 percent cooked, then drain.
Spread half the rice over the chicken, scatter half the fried onions and mint, then add the rest of the rice.
Top with the remaining onions, mint and [[2 tbsp]] ghee, then cover with a tight lid.
Cook on very low heat for 25 minutes (dum), then rest for 10 minutes.
Gently fold and serve with raita.

ing: grated, plus extra matchsticks to garnish
st: Heat [[0.5 cup]] ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onions for 12 minutes until golden brown.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook 2 minutes.
Add the beef, chili, coriander, turmeric and [[2 tsp]] salt and brown for 8 minutes.
Pour in [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 3 hours until the meat falls off the bone.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] flour with [[0.5 cup]] cold water into a smooth slurry.
Stir the slurry slowly into the stew and cook 15 minutes until the gravy is thick.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] garam masala and simmer 5 minutes.
Serve topped with ginger matchsticks, cilantro and lemon, with naan.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] oil in a wok or wide pan over medium-high heat.
Add the cumin seeds and garlic and fry for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and sear for 8 minutes until browned.
Add the tomatoes, chili powder, coriander and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Cook uncovered, stirring often, for 20 minutes until the tomatoes break down and oil separates.
Check that the chicken has reached 165°F (74°C).
Add the green chilies and half the ginger, cooking 5 minutes more.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] garam masala, the remaining ginger and cilantro and serve with naan.
Rinse the soaked wheat, lentils, dal and barley and combine in a large pot with [[10 cups]] water.
Add the beef, half the ginger and garlic, turmeric and [[2 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, skim, cover and simmer for 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until everything is very soft and the beef reaches at least 145°F (63°C).
Meanwhile, fry the onions in [[0.33 cup]] ghee for 15 minutes until golden brown.
Mash the stew vigorously with a wooden spoon or hand blender until thick and stringy.
Add the remaining ginger, garlic, chili powder and [[2 tsp]] garam masala.
Cook 30 more minutes on low, adding hot water if too thick.
Serve topped with fried onions and lemon.
Combine the beef, onion, ginger, garlic, chili, cilantro, garam masala, cumin, chili powder and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Knead for 5 minutes until the mixture is sticky and well combined.
Cover and chill for 30 minutes.
Wet your hands, take a handful of meat and press it around a skewer in a long sausage shape.
Heat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat and brush with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Grill the kebabs for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and they reach 160°F (71°C).
Serve with chutney, onion rings and naan.
Mix the beef, onion, tomato, crushed coriander seeds, chilies, egg, cilantro, [[2 tbsp]] cornmeal, chili flakes and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Knead well by hand for 5 minutes.
Chill for 30 minutes so the patties hold together.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten each into a wide thin patty, about half an inch thick.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side until deeply browned and they reach 160°F (71°C).
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with naan and chutney.
Place the mustard greens and spinach in a pot with [[1 cup]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes until the greens are very soft.
Blend or mash the greens coarsely.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] cornmeal and simmer 10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] butter in a small pan and cook the onion, garlic, ginger and chilies for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir the butter mixture into the greens.
Simmer 5 minutes and serve with flatbread.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] warm milk, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and the yeast and let stand 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl combine [[3.5 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] baking powder.
Add the yeast mixture, [[0.5 cup]] yogurt and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and mix into a dough.
Knead 8 minutes until smooth and soft.
Cover and rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 6 balls and roll each into an oval about quarter inch thick.
Heat a cast iron skillet on high heat until very hot.
Cook each naan 1 to 2 minutes per side until puffed with charred spots.
Brush with the remaining melted butter and serve warm.

ing: plus extra for dusting; atta if you have it
st: Mix [[2 cups]] flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Add [[0.75 cup]] warm water slowly and knead for 8 minutes into a soft dough.
Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls and roll each into a thin circle.
Brush with melted ghee and fold into a half circle, brush again and fold into a triangle.
Roll the triangle out to about quarter inch thick.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook each paratha for 2 minutes per side.
Brush with oil and ghee and cook until golden and flaky, about 2 minutes more.
Serve hot with yogurt or curry.

ing: plus 4 tbsp for dough and filling
st: Mix [[2 cups]] flour, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[4 tbsp]] oil until crumbly.
Add about [[0.5 cup]] cold water and knead into a stiff dough, then rest 30 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil, add the cumin seeds, onion and chilies and cook 4 minutes.
Add the potatoes, peas, coriander, garam masala and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook 5 minutes. Mash lightly and cool.
Divide the dough into 6 balls and roll each into an oval, then cut in half.
Shape each half into a cone, fill with potato and seal the edge with water.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 340°F (170°C).
Fry in batches for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with chutney.
Boil [[2 cups]] sugar, [[2 cups]] water and the cardamom for 8 minutes, then stir in [[1 tsp]] rosewater and keep warm.
Mix the milk powder, [[0.25 cup]] flour and baking soda.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] ghee and enough milk to form a soft, smooth dough, without kneading too much.
Cover the dough and rest for 10 minutes.
Roll into 16 small smooth balls with no cracks.
Heat [[3 cups]] ghee or oil to 275°F (135°C), a gentle low heat.
Fry the balls in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring gently, until deep golden brown.
Drop the hot jamun into the warm syrup.
Soak for at least 1 hour before serving.

ing: for sweet lassi; use salt and cumin for salty
st: Add the yogurt to a blender.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] cold milk.
Add [[3 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.25 tsp]] cardamom.
Add the ice cubes to the blender.
Blend for 1 minute until frothy and smooth.
Taste and adjust sweetness.
Pour into tall glasses and serve at once.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a pot over medium. Fry the onion 8 minutes until deep golden.
Add [[1 tbsp]] ginger garlic paste and [[1 tsp]] cumin. Stir for 1 minute until the raw smell goes.
Add the ground beef, breaking it up. Cook 8 minutes until browned with no pink left.
Stir in [[1 tsp]] coriander, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] chili powder, salt and the tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes until jammy.
Add the potatoes and [[1 cup]] water. Cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Uncover and cook to thicken, then stir in [[1 tsp]] garam masala and the cilantro. Serve with roti.
nt: Best swap: ground chicken or crumbled paneer for beef 1:1; cook 12 minutes in a pressure cooker.

st: Mix the flour, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, [[1 tbsp]] ghee and about [[0.5 cup]] warm water into a firm, smooth dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Simmer the chickpeas with the cumin, turmeric, remaining salt and [[1 cup]] water for 15 minutes, mashing some against the pan to thicken the curry.
For the halwa, bring the sugar, water and cardamom to a simmer. In another pan, toast the semolina in [[0.25 cup]] ghee over medium heat for 5 minutes until golden and nutty.
Pour the syrup into the semolina carefully; it will spit. Stir over low heat for 3 minutes until it thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
Divide the dough into 12 balls and roll each into a 4 inch round, thin and even.
Heat the oil to 375°F. Slide in one puri and press gently with a spoon so it puffs, then fry 30 seconds per side until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Serve the puris hot with the chickpea curry and the halwa on the side.
nt: Deep fried bread, simmered curry, stirred halwa
Best swap: use whole wheat flour for half the flour for a more rustic puri, or neutral oil in place of ghee for the halwa.

st: Simmer the sugar and [[2 cup]] water for 8 minutes into a thin syrup. Keep warm.
Whisk the flour with [[1 cup]] water and the milk into a smooth, lump free slurry.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] ghee in a heavy pan over low heat. Add the slurry and the cardamom, stirring nonstop.
Pour in the hot syrup slowly and keep stirring for 30 minutes as the mix thickens and darkens to caramel brown.
Add the remaining ghee a little at a time and keep stirring for 25 minutes until it turns glossy and leaves the sides.
Stir in the saffron milk and half the almonds and pistachios.
Spread in a greased tray, top with the remaining nuts and press in. Set for 2 hours, then cut in squares.
nt: Best swap: use cornstarch for half of the flour for a lighter texture; use coconut oil for ghee.
